main_text.l: Qui fit, quòd ignes quidam proij-
ciuntur deorsum?
Omnis quidem ignis natura sursum enitítur: at-
tamen meteora quaedam ignita proijciuntur deor-
sum, quòd supra exhalatione pendeant fumi quidam
concreti, humiditatis & frigiditatis nonnihil in se
habentes. Quamuis hic aliquàdo auxiliatur aliquo
modo exhalationum pondus ac densitas.
Qui fit, quòd quidam ignes post ac-
censionem mouentur in di-
uersas partes?
Mouentur in obliquum ac saltant quidam ignes
duabus de causis. 1. A natura omnes eluctantur
sursum, siue recta, siue in latus. 2. Vi autem mo-
uentur deorsum, siue recta, siue in latus. Prouenit
autem hæc uis à materia humida & frigida, super-
nè occurrente. Natura ac uis motus causa existunt.
Quae sunt causae phasmatum, ac diuer-
forum colorum in sublimi
apparentium?
Causa formalis: Duobus modis colores in exha-
lationes inducuntur. 1. Quando alicubi ignis
siue lumen in sublimi existit, verum inter illud &
nostrum aspectum exhalationes quaedam bene com-
pactae suspensae hærent, tum quidem necesse est in
ipsis ipsis

marginalia.note: I. Causa materialis, siccae atq; aridae exhalationes.

page.notes: The long s is read as s throughout ("sursum", "saltant", "existunt"), since the scan's f-like letter has no crossbar. The bullet mark before "uersas" is a printer's mark, not text. The summary lines I. and II. stand in the left margin with the marginal label "Libro I. cap.5."; the second summary line is partly in the column, so its position is doubtful. The last line "ipsis" stands alone at the right. The page number "502" is read from a worn scan and may need checking. The running head "AND. HYPERII" is also read from a worn scan. The reading "ipsis ipsis" in the final paragraph is doubtful: the last word on the scan is a single "ipsis" and the duplicate should be checked.
